title: Handle vocabulary
description: The words every public handle is drawn from, and how handles are normalised for lookup. Loaded by pseudonym-service at startup; there is no second copy of these lists in code. Handles are permanent and always drawn — members cannot supply their own.

number_max.description: Capped at six digits because HANDLE_PATTERN accepts \d{4,6}. Widening past this makes every new handle fail validation.

normalise.description: Defines the uniqueness key and what account recovery matches on. A transcription aid: somebody typing their handle has usually copied it off paper, having lost their phone.

confusables.description: Single character to single character. No target may also be a source, or normalisation is not idempotent and the unique index stops being a key. pseudonym-service verifies this at startup.

wordList.description: Handles are permanent, so adjectives x nouns x numbers is a hard ceiling on total accounts, not a collision budget. pseudonym-service refuses to start if that product falls under 100,000,000; the minItems floor here is the schema-level half of the same guard. No word may appear in both lists.

items.description: Capitalised, letters only, 3-12 characters — anything else produces a handle that fails HANDLE_PATTERN. Nothing that reads as a mood, diagnosis, verdict, body, injury, religion, caste, politics or brand; see the header of handle-words.v1.yaml.
